capability: Shorten 1.1.12 startup catalog loading: deduplicate schema validation, parsing and compilation, and preload built-in bundles in bounded dependency layers
searchEvidence: Owner decisions 9 to 11 (2026-09-25): startup optimization is the 1.1.12 product priority; memory must not regress against the v1.1.11 package shape; the commander may implement bounded parallel bundle loading under an ADR 0049 amendment. On 2026-09-25 the owner also directed parallel work wherever possible with no race condition.

Package-shape measurement and a sampled thread-time trace located the startup gap in the required catalog stage: built-in bundle loading, dominated by Draft 2020-12 schema meta-validation and instance evaluation, repeated parsing and repeated compilation, all serial on one worker thread.

Existing owners are extended, not duplicated: ProfileBundleSchemaValidator and ProfileBundleLoader own bundle trust checks; BuiltInV2Bundle owns each bundle's lazy catalog; BuiltInV2Registration and CtrlRamV2RouteRegistry own compilation and CtrlRAM report metadata; CanonicalCapabilityCatalogSource owns the serial catalog pass. Units 1 to 3 were implemented earlier under the bounded local R1 path (WS-PERF log); this record admits them with the R2 preload for integration.
semanticOwner: ProfileBundleSchemaValidator and ProfileBundleLoader remain the only bundle trust gateway; BuiltInV2Bundle's lazy catalog remains the only bundle catalog; CanonicalCapabilityCatalogSource's serial pass remains the only publisher of routes, progress and errors.
terminalContract: Keep every published route, fingerprint, plan, disclosure, selector publication, progress sequence, first error, issue code and message identical for the fixed built-in inputs, pinned by a complete catalog snapshot digest. Units 1 to 3 reuse only verdicts and compilations of identical inputs, never cache failures, and keep CtrlRAM definitions per load. The preload follows ADR 0075: fixed dependency layers with barriers, one serial warm-up bundle, at most min(4, ProcessorCount - 1) workers, no cross-worker waiting, failures left to the serial pass, cancellation propagated after started bundles finish, and serial loading when the trust index names a bundle outside the layer table. Concurrent evaluation of shared JsonSchema instances is used only with a source-level audit of JsonSchema.Net 8.0.5; otherwise workers use their own schema instances. Adoption requires per-launch package-shape memory within the v1.1.11 baseline and GC heap after warm-up at most 50 MB. No change to profiles, contracts, schemas, firmware bytes, ranges, package settings or the first-window path.

designReview.evidence: 2026-09-25 two independent read-only design reviews of ADR 0075 (draft and revision, both ACCEPT-WITH-CHANGES). Incorporated: equivalence limited to fixed re-readable inputs with the accepted process-lifetime failure cache pinned by test; dependency layers with barriers and a serial warm-up instead of a general acyclicity argument, with the layer table pinned against the recomputed reference graph; per-launch memory gates; precise cancellation and failure precedence; ordered-slot parallel computation evaluated per stage and deferred with reasons; shared JsonSchema evaluation admitted only with a source-level library audit, else per-worker isolation. Units 1 to 3 are bounded R1 corrections already tested locally; the final review covers them with the preload.
